newsitem.title: USA: US bankruptcies hit new record in Q2 -- institute.
newsitem.headline: US bankruptcies hit new record in Q2 -- institute.

text.p: U.S. bankruptcy filings rose 12 percent to a new all-time high of 297,162 in the second quarter of 1996, the American Bankruptcy Institute said on Wednesday in a statement.
Quoting statistics from the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, it said the previous record was set in the first quarter of 1996, when bankruptcy filings totaled 266,149.
The second quarter filings pushed the total number of filings in the 12-month period ended June 30, 1996 to over one million, reaching 1,042,110.

"Today's bankruptcy boom is the natural result of three years of sustained consumer spending increases that far outpaced income growth," said Sam Gerdano, executive director of the American Bankruptcy Institute.
Personal bankruptcies accounted for 95.3 percent of the total number of filings in the second quarter.
